name: External-repo harvest — clone an open-source repo, mine transferable wins for agentruntime, card the adoptions
description: Generalizes the grok-build exploration into reusable machinery: point it at any open-source repo and it clones it, maps what the repo IS, fans out 3 harvester lanes (each through a distinct lens — architecture/data-model, novel techniques, interfaces/DX), and a synthesis tier ranks the highest-value ADOPTIONS given what agentruntime already has. HONEST BY DESIGN: every lane must check OUR tree before claiming a gap ('assume it exists until search proves otherwise' — chrono/task-graph were both re-found after being assumed missing); a win we already have is dropped, not carded. Findings land on the genesis board (collapse_key harvest-<slug>-*) for human triage — NOT auto-adopted. Params (ALL REQUIRED — an unfilled param passes through literally and fails loudly, same contract as divergent-reasoning-custom): repoUrl (git URL to clone), slug (short kebab name — names the temp clone dir + genesis collapse_keys), focus (prose: which agentruntime capability this repo maps to, e.g. 'our memory/graph stack: packages/memory, repo-memory, graph, genesis'), curatorModel (harvester+synthesis tier, e.g. claude-opus-4-8 — verification quality is model-dependent), notify (who gets the summary, e.g. claude). Standard invocation: POST /workflow {"workflow":"external-repo-harvest","async":true,"params":{"repoUrl":"https://github.com/owner/repo","slug":"repo","focus":"...","curatorModel":"claude-opus-4-8","notify":"claude"}}. Windows host: the clone node uses cmd syntax + D:/tmp.

params.command: rmdir /s /q D:\tmp\harvest-{{params.slug}} 2>nul & git clone --depth 1 {{params.repoUrl}} D:\tmp\harvest-{{params.slug}} & git -C D:\tmp\harvest-{{params.slug}} ls-files

meta.description: Shallow-clone the target repo to D:/tmp/harvest-<slug>; stdout is its ls-files tree for the mapper. NOTE: do NOT use `if exist PATH cmd & next` — on Windows CMD, when PATH is missing the false IF skips the rest of the line including `& git clone`, so the node exits 0 with empty stdout and no tree (wf-1784891327668-vnljg2, 34ms no-op). Always rmdir (2>nul) then clone.

params.prompt:
You are the MAPPER of an external-repo harvest. The repo is cloned at D:/tmp/harvest-{{params.slug}} (READ it with your tools). Our interest — what to mine it FOR: {{params.focus}}.

Its file tree:
{{nodes.clone.result.stdout}}

Actively read its README, top-level package/module layout, and 3-5 of its most load-bearing source files. Produce a tight MAP for the harvester lanes: (1) what this project IS in 2-3 sentences; (2) its 4-6 most distinctive/novel pieces (data model, core algorithm, interfaces, storage, orchestration) with the real file paths where each lives; (3) the single most important thing it does that our focus area might learn from. Be concrete and cite real cloned-repo paths. This map grounds the lanes — do not editorialize about adoption yet.

meta.description: Reads the cloned repo, produces a grounded map (what it is + its distinctive pieces + paths) for the lanes.

params.prompt:
You are HARVESTER LANE 1 — LENS: ARCHITECTURE & DATA MODEL. The external repo is cloned at D:/tmp/harvest-{{params.slug}}; your cwd is the agentruntime monorepo. Focus: {{params.focus}}.

MAP:
{{nodes.map.result.reply}}

Through your lens (how it structures data / schema / storage / graph / retrieval), find 2-4 TRANSFERABLE WINS — things about its architecture or data model that would strengthen agentruntime's focus area. For EACH win:
1. Read the actual cloned-repo code that implements it (cite file:line).
2. HONESTY GATE (what makes you a harvester, not a hype machine): search OUR tree for whether agentruntime ALREADY has this — 'assume it exists until search proves otherwise' (chrono and task-graph were both re-found after being assumed missing). If we already have it, DROP the win (or reframe as a concrete improvement to what we have, citing our file). A win we already have, carded as new, is worse than none.
3. ROUTE each survivor: adopt-now (clear + high-value) | prototype (promising, needs a spike) | note (interesting, not now) | drop.
4. CARD IT: write a JSON file {"tag":"@agentruntime/genesis:capture","caller":"external-repo-harvest","payload":{"agent":"harvest-{{params.slug}}-arch","source":"conversation","collapse_key":"harvest-{{params.slug}}-arch","title":"Harvest ({{params.slug}}/arch): <n> transferable win(s)","why":"External-repo harvest, honesty-gated against our tree; for triage, NOT auto-adopted.","note":"<one line per win: [route] title — THEIRS: repo/path.py:line — OURS: agentruntime/path.ts (have?/gap) — value>"}} then POST it: curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:39827/emit-event -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data-binary @<file>. Confirm genesis is in observers.
5. Reply with a compact digest: wins table (title | THEIR ref | do-we-have-it? | route | value), an honest 'checked-and-dropped (already have)' list, and card-posted confirmation.

meta.description: Lane 1 — architecture/data-model lens, honesty-gated against our tree.
